legend: After studying the "Matrix Bel Lotus", Muhannad (not you, Nahhal) invented a new concept in numbers, the lotusency. The lotusency of an integer Y%%ZSMJ0%% is the number of times it can be square-rooted while still remaining an integer. For example:
Lotusency of 5%%ZSMJ7%% is 0%%ZSMJ8%% because its square-root is not an integer.
Muhannad has an integer X%%ZSMJ9%%, and he wants to maximize its lotusency. He can do the following operation at most K%%ZSMJ10%% times:
Choose any prime number p%%ZSMJ11%% and set X=X⋅p%%ZSMJ12%%.
What is the maximum lotusency he can obtain?
input: The first line contains a single integer tc(1≤tc≤2⋅105)%%ZSMJ13%% — the number of testcases.
The first and only line of each testcase consists of two integers X,K(2≤X≤2⋅105)(0≤K≤1018)%%ZSMJ14%%.
output: For each testcase, print a single integer, the maximum lotusency Muhannad can obtain.
